NO currency year is stated anywhere in P09 (Tables 4, 5, 8, 10 and the text are all 'USD'). Loaded rows use 2013_USD, the brief's publication year (December 2013), as a flagged judgement. The underlying sources date from 2006 to 2013.

Main file: the wood pellet mill (pellet-plant_biomass, candidate archetype pellet-plant_wood) and torrefaction with pelletising (reactor_biomass_torrefaction, candidate reactor_torrefaction) - NOT the iron-ore pellet-plant archetypes. Four processes: Table 4 (Examples 1 and 2 as one example, cases tagged [Example 1], [Example 2], [Example 2, upscaled]); Table 5 (sawdust plant, 40,000 t/yr: capex, maintenance, capacity factor 91%, step lifetimes 10-20 yr, 0.41 GJ/t); the Table 10 summary block (capex and energy by feedstock, tagged [sawdust] etc.); and text p.7 input ratios. Capex is DERIVED per t/yr from the printed totals (MUSD or kUSD) and capacities of the same case. Energy use is recorded as ELECTRICITY flows by judgement (drying heat is not given anywhere as a per-t figure; p.7 gives 1200 kWh per t of water evaporated). O&M given as % of investment is in the capex notes and the _pellet-plant-details sidecar. Sidecars (not loaded): _pellet-plant-details (full Tables 4 and 5, product properties, staff, O&M %), _supply-costs (feedstock supply costs, prices, cost shares - agriculture and forestry supply, out of scope), _transport (Table 8 - out of scope), _feedstock-properties (Tables 1, 3), _potentials (Table 6, Table 10 potentials), _life-cycle (Table 9 EU default factors, not Scope 1), _context (reactor and process temperatures, drying energy per t water, trade). Out of scope and not extracted: harvesting, baling, chipping in the field, storage, pipelines.

(1) Table 4 labels tonnages 'Mt' (feedstock intake, output capacity, 'GJ/Mt') although the values are tonnes. (2) Table 5 'Maintenance (kUSD/t pellets)' holds USD/t (225 kUSD/yr / 40,000 t = 5.6). (3) Table 5 title 'utilization uactor'. (4) Table 10 heads maintenance 'kUSD/t pellet-yr' but prints '5% invest cost' and '7% invest cost'. (5) O&M share of investment conflicts: Table 4 Example 2 1.8%/y (wood pellets), Table 5 225/4866 = 4.6%, Table 10 5%. (6) Table 10 'Mass Efficiency' 1 for pellets vs Table 4 Example 2 input/output 1.01/1. (7) Table 10 log wood investment 0.251 lies above the printed range 0.07-0.25. (8) Table 5 annualized investment follows no single rule (drying 1235/10/40000 = 3.1 but storage 1408/20/40000 = 1.8 vs 2.9 printed). (9) Energy-use figures never say which carrier; they match electricity (Table 4) and exclude drying heat. (10) No currency year anywhere. (11) Table 3: torrefied pellets typical bulk density 750 at the bottom of its range (750-850); wood pellets energy density 11 at the top of (7.5-11.0). (12) Table 9 row order: EU-temperate/natural-gas pellets (35) sits among the tropical rows. (13) Table 10 lists 'Woodchips from Scandinavian forest residues' twice (with and without transport). (14) Typos: 'Giant read', 'shreeding', 'loafing', 'bay a number', 'Transporation', 'rangeUSD'.
